title: Create and Work on an Isolated Feature Branch
description: Create a new branch `feature/profile-page`, add a new file on that branch, and observe how switching branches updates your workspace in real-time.
steps: In `hcc-git-practice`, make sure you are on `main`: `git switch main` (or `git checkout main`)
Create and switch to a new feature branch: `git switch -c feature/profile-page`
Verify your active branch: `git branch` (notice the asterisk `*` next to `feature/profile-page`)

Create a new file `profile.md` with: `# User Profile

Name: HCC Learner`
Stage and commit: `git add profile.md && git commit -m "feat: create user profile page"`
Now switch back to `main`: `git switch main`
Look in your file explorer / folder — notice `profile.md` completely vanished! It's safe on your feature branch
Switch back to the feature branch: `git switch feature/profile-page` — `profile.md` reappears instantly!
expected_output: You can seamlessly switch between branches and observe Git restoring file states to match the active branch.
tips: Modern Git (v2.23+) introduced `git switch` specifically for changing branches, replacing the overloaded `git checkout`.
Always commit or stash your working edits before switching branches so Git doesn't block the switch.
